$meta.title: Kernal jump table
$meta.description: Every published entry point, in slot order, plus the reserved range.
$meta.warning: Generated file — edit the BIOS source and re-run the extractor, not this.

reserved.behavior: Each reserved slot jumps to UnimplementedStub, which is a bare RTS.

groups: General output utilities (console = IO_MODE-routed via Chrout)

slots.name: Chrout
slots.description: Chrout dispatcher — routes output based on IO_MODE
input: A = character to output

slots.name: Chrin
slots.description: Get a character from the INPUT_BUFFER if available
notes: On return, carry flag indicates whether a character was available
If character available the character will be in the A register

slots.name: WriteBuffer
slots.description: Write a character from the A register to the INPUT_BUFFER

slots.name: ReadBuffer
slots.description: Read a character from the INPUT_BUFFER and store it in A register
notes: Every reader comes through here — Chrin, BASIC's line input, INKEY, the break
check, a cartridge — so this is where RTS is lowered again once the buffer has
drained. A reader that skipped it would leave a terminal with RTS/CTS flow
control waiting for good.

slots.name: BufferSize
slots.description: Return in A register the number of unread bytes in the INPUT_BUFFER

slots.name: SetIOMode
slots.description: Set IO_MODE
input: A = mode (bit 0: 0=video, 1=serial)

slots.name: GetIOMode
slots.description: Get IO_MODE
output: A = current IO_MODE

slots.name: InitVideo
slots.summary: Text-mode console: registers, the card's font, palette row 0
slots.description: Put the PICOVDP in the Kernal's Text-mode console
notes: Writes the register table below with the display off, has the card reload its
font into the pattern table at $0800 (VdpLoadFont, a frame at most), restores
palette row 0, sets the border
from VID_PEN and turns the display on.  It does not clear the screen: the
name and attribute tables are left as they were and shown unscrolled.  A
program that switched modes, moved tables or overwrote the glyphs gets the
console back with this one call.
Skips silently if no video card is fitted

slots.name: VideoClear
slots.description: Fill the screen with spaces in the current pen, cursor home
notes: Fills the 960-byte name table at VRAM $0000 with $20 and the 960 attributes at
$0400 with VID_PEN, so COLOR fg,bg : CLS gives a screen of that color, and
takes the scroll origin back to row 0.
Skips silently if no video card is fitted

slots.name: VideoPutChar
slots.description: Write a character at VID_CURSOR_ADDR, colored with VID_PEN
input: A = character to write

slots.name: VideoSetCursor
slots.description: Set cursor position
input: X = column (0-39), Y = row (0-23), on the screen as shown
notes: VID_CURSOR_ADDR = ((Y + VID_TOP) mod 24) * 40 + X, the cell's place in the
name table once the scroll origin is folded in
Skips silently if no video card is fitted

slots.name: VideoGetCursor
slots.description: Get cursor position
output: X = column (0-39), Y = row (0-23)

slots.name: VideoScroll
slots.description: Scroll the screen up one line, in hardware
notes: Moves the display origin down a row (VID_TOP, and L0SCRY = VID_TOP * 8) and
blanks the row that was at the top, which is now the bottom line, in the
current pen.  The name table does not move.  The cursor keeps its screen
position, so its VRAM address is worked out again.
Skips silently if no video card is fitted

slots.name: VideoSetColor
slots.summary: Set the pen and the border (A = fg<<4 | bg)
slots.description: Set the pen for later output, and the border
input: A = fg<<4 | bg.  VID_PEN = A, and register 7 = A, so the border follows
notes: the background.  Characters already on screen keep their colors.
Skips silently if no video card is fitted

slots.name: VideoChroutRaw
slots.summary: Output char to video (raw, no control-code handling)
slots.description: Output character to video (raw, no control-code handling)
input: A = character code (0-255)
notes: Always writes the character glyph at the cursor position and advances.
Preserves: A, X, Y

slots.name: InitSID
slots.description: Initialze the Sound Card (6581)

slots.name: Beep
slots.description: Play a short beep sound
notes: Uses SidPlayNote on voice 0 with ~475 Hz tone, then silences
Skips silently if SID is absent

slots.name: SidPlayNote
slots.description: Play a note on a SID voice
input: A = voice (0-2), X = frequency low byte, Y = frequency high byte
notes: Uses triangle waveform with standard ADSR (Attack=0, Decay=9, Sustain=A, Release=2)
Skips silently if no SID is fitted

slots.name: SidSilence
slots.description: Silence all 3 SID voices
notes: Gates off all voices, letting the release phase of the envelope ring out.
The frequency registers are deliberately left alone. Zeroing them stops the
oscillator dead, which freezes the waveform at whatever level it had reached
and leaves the envelope to decay a DC offset instead of a tone — an audible
thump at the end of every note. Gate off is all the SID needs; the envelope
takes the voice to zero on its own.
Skips silently if no SID is fitted

slots.name: SidSetVolume
slots.description: Set SID master volume
input: A = volume (0-15); upper nibble of SID_MODE_VOL is cleared (no filter)
notes: Skips silently if no SID is fitted

slots.name: FsLoadFile
slots.description: Load file from CF into PROGRAM_START ($0800)
input: STR_PTR ($02-$03) points to null-terminated filename
output: Carry clear = success, FS_FILE_SIZE = bytes loaded
Carry set = file not found or read error
modifies: Flags, A, X, Y, CF_LBA, CF_BUF_PTR

slots.name: FsSaveFile
slots.description: Save data from PROGRAM_START to CF
input: STR_PTR ($02-$03) points to null-terminated filename
FS_FILE_SIZE ($034A-$034B) = number of bytes to save
output: Carry clear = success, Carry set = error (directory full or write error)
modifies: Flags, A, X, Y, CF_LBA, CF_BUF_PTR

slots.name: FsDeleteFile
slots.description: Delete a file from the CompactFlash filesystem
input: STR_PTR ($02-$03) points to null-terminated filename
output: Carry clear = success, Carry set = file not found or error
modifies: Flags, A, X, Y, CF_LBA, CF_BUF_PTR

slots.name: InitKB
slots.description: Initialize the Keyboard via VIA (IO 6)
notes: Configures Port B (matrix) and Port A (PS/2) as inputs
CB2 low (enable matrix encoder), CA2 low (enable PS/2 encoder)
CB1 and CA1 falling-edge IRQs enabled

slots.name: ReadJoystick1
slots.description: Read joystick 1 on Port B
output: A = joystick bitmask (active-low bits: R-L-D-U-Y-X-B-A)
notes: Disables both encoders, waits for release, then reads the raw port directly —
the same way a C64 reads a CIA port. No sei/PCR save-restore is needed: the port
is static while the encoders are off and no interrupt handler touches these ports.

slots.name: ReadJoystick2
slots.description: Read joystick 2 on Port A
output: A = joystick bitmask (active-low bits: R-L-D-U-Y-X-B-A)

slots.name: InitSC
slots.description: Initialize the Serial Card (6551)

slots.name: SerialChrout
slots.description: Output a character from the A register to the Serial Card
notes: TIC 00 turns the transmitter off as well as raising RTS, so a character
written while the BIOS is holding RTS up would never leave: the loop below
would spin on a TDRE that cannot come. RTS is therefore dropped for the byte
and put back afterwards if the buffer is still full, and interrupts are held
off meanwhile so that Irq cannot raise it again mid-character.

slots.name: XModemLoad
slots.description: Receive data via standard XModem protocol
input: XFER_PTR = destination address (set by caller)
output: Carry clear = success, XFER_PTR past last byte written
XFER_REMAIN = total bytes received
Carry set = transfer failed

slots.name: XModemSave
slots.description: Send data via standard XModem protocol
input: XFER_PTR = source address, XFER_REMAIN = byte count (set by caller)
output: Carry clear = success, Carry set = transfer failed

slots.name: RtcReadTime
slots.description: Read current time from DS1511Y
output: A = hours (binary), X = minutes (binary), Y = seconds (binary)

slots.name: RtcReadDate
slots.description: Read current date from DS1511Y
output: A = day of month (binary), X = month (binary), Y = year (binary)
RTC_BUF_CENT = century (binary)

slots.name: RtcWriteTime
slots.description: Set DS1511Y time
input: A = hours (binary), X = minutes (binary), Y = seconds (binary)

slots.name: RtcWriteDate
slots.description: Set DS1511Y date
input: A = day of month (binary), X = month (binary), Y = year (binary)
RTC_BUF_CENT = century (binary)

slots.name: RtcReadNVRAM
slots.description: Read a byte from DS1511Y NVRAM
input: X = NVRAM address ($00-$FF)
output: A = data byte

slots.name: RtcWriteNVRAM
slots.description: Write a byte to DS1511Y NVRAM
input: X = NVRAM address ($00-$FF), A = data byte

slots.name: StReadSector
slots.description: Read one 512-byte sector from CompactFlash
input: CF_LBA ($26-$29) = LBA address, CF_BUF_PTR ($24-$25) = destination pointer
output: Carry clear = success, Carry set = error
CF_BUF_PTR advanced by 512 bytes on success

slots.name: StWriteSector
slots.description: Write one 512-byte sector to CompactFlash
input: CF_LBA ($26-$29) = LBA address, CF_BUF_PTR ($24-$25) = source pointer
output: Carry clear = success, Carry set = error
CF_BUF_PTR advanced by 512 bytes on success

slots.name: StWaitReady
slots.description: Wait for CompactFlash to become ready
output: Carry clear = ready, Carry set = error or timeout
notes: Polls ST_STATUS until BSY=0 and RDY=1, with X/Y timeout (~65536 iterations)

slots.name: SysDelay
slots.description: Delay for a specified number of centiseconds
input: A = count low byte, X = count high byte
modifies: Flags, A, X, Y (X/Y clobbered only in software-fallback path)
notes: Uses VIA T1 in one-shot mode. 9999 cycles @ 1MHz = ~10ms per tick.

slots.name: KernalInit
slots.summary: Initialize all hardware (caller must reset SP; no cli); rts when done
slots.description: Initialize RAM variables, probe & init all hardware
notes: Sets HW_PRESENT, IO_MODE, IRQ/BRK/NMI pointers, BOOT_VECTOR=0
Does NOT enable interrupts (caller must cli)
Does NOT reset the stack pointer (caller should do this before JSR)
Does NOT print anything or start BASIC

slots.name: KernalVersion
slots.description: Return BIOS version in registers
output: A = major version, X = minor version

slots.name: FsLoadFileAddr
slots.description: Load named file to FS_IO_ADDR (caller preset)
input: STR_PTR = filename, FS_IO_ADDR = destination address

slots.name: FsSaveFileAddr
slots.summary: Save FS_FILE_SIZE bytes from FS_IO_ADDR to named file
slots.description: Save FS_FILE_SIZE bytes from FS_IO_ADDR to named file
input: STR_PTR = filename, FS_IO_ADDR = source address, FS_FILE_SIZE = byte count

slots.name: FsFormatDisk
slots.summary: Zero the current disk's directory sector
slots.description: Zero the current disk's directory sector (erases its file list)
output: Carry clear = success, Carry set = write error
modifies: Flags, A, X, Y, CF_LBA, CF_BUF_PTR

slots.name: FsSetDisk
slots.description: Select the current CF disk bank
input: A = disk number (0-255)

slots.name: FsGetDisk
slots.description: Get the current CF disk bank
output: A = current disk number

slots.name: FsPrintDisk
slots.description: Print "DISK n" (decimal) + CRLF via Chrout
modifies: Flags, A, X, Y, FS_FILE_SIZE, FS_DIR_IDX

slots.name: PrintStr
slots.group: General output utilities (console = IO_MODE-routed via Chrout)
slots.summary: Print NUL-terminated string (A=lo, Y=hi); clobbers A,Y,STR_PTR
slots.description: Print a NUL-terminated string to the console (routed by IO_MODE
input: A = string address low, Y = string address high
output: A, Y clobbered; X preserved; clobbers STR_PTR (Chrout preserves it)
notes: through Chrout, so it works for video OR serial).  General-purpose; used by
BASIC (via the BasPrintStr alias) and available to cartridges.

slots.name: PrintCRLF
slots.group: General output utilities (console = IO_MODE-routed via Chrout)
slots.description: Emit CR ($0D) then LF ($0A) via Chrout.

slots.name: PrintDecU16
slots.group: General output utilities (console = IO_MODE-routed via Chrout)
slots.summary: Print unsigned 16-bit decimal (A=lo, X=hi), no leading zeros
slots.description: Print an unsigned 16-bit value as decimal (no leading zeros).
input: A = value low, X = value high
modifies: Flags, A, X, Y, FS_FILE_SIZE (consumed), FS_DIR_IDX
notes: General-purpose console output; used by BASIC (line numbers) and available
to cartridges.  Shares the FsPrintSize core below.

slots.name: KBDisable
slots.summary: Release both encoders and settle; ports free for raw read
slots.description: Disable both keyboard encoders and wait for them to release the ports
notes: Sets CB2/CA2 high, then busy-waits so the encoder firmware has time to let go of
both ports before the caller reads them. Self-contained cycle loop — deliberately
not SysDelay or the VIA T1 path, so it is safe to call while the caller owns the timers.

slots.name: KBEnable
slots.description: Re-enable both keyboard encoders
notes: Sets CB2 low (enable matrix encoder) and CA2 low (enable PS/2 encoder)

slots.name: NvStat
slots.description: Report a slot's state
input: X = slot (0-15)
output: A = NV_EMPTY / NV_VALID / NV_BAD, Y = owner ID, C clear
C set on no RTC or bad slot (A, Y undefined)
modifies: Flags (D and I preserved), A, Y

slots.name: NvRead
slots.summary: Copy a valid slot's payload (X=slot, A/Y=dest lo/hi)
slots.description: Copy a valid slot's 14 payload bytes to the caller's buffer
input: X = slot (0-15), A/Y = destination lo/hi
output: A = status, Y = owner ID; C clear and the buffer written only if A = NV_VALID
C set on no RTC or bad slot (A, Y undefined), or a slot that is not valid (A = its status, Y = its owner ID) — the buffer is untouched
modifies: Flags (D and I preserved), A, Y, NV_PTR

slots.name: NvWrite
slots.summary: Write a slot (X=slot, A/Y=src lo/hi, NV_ID=owner ID)
slots.description: Write a slot: owner ID, checksum and 14 payload bytes
input: X = slot (0-15), A/Y = source lo/hi, NV_ID = owner ID ($01-$FF)
output: C clear; C set on no RTC, bad slot, or NV_ID = 0 (nothing written)
modifies: Flags (D and I preserved), A, Y, NV_PTR

slots.name: NvErase
slots.summary: Zero all 16 bytes of a slot (X=slot)
slots.description: Zero all 16 bytes of a slot, so nothing of the old save is legible
input: X = slot (0-15)
output: C clear; C set on no RTC or bad slot

slots.name: NvFind
slots.summary: Lowest slot owned by A ($00 = first free) → X
slots.description: Find the lowest slot whose owner ID is A
input: A = owner ID
output: X = slot, C clear; C set if no slot matched (X undefined)
notes: Matches any non-free slot, valid or damaged; A = $00 finds the lowest free slot.

slots.name: NvFormat
slots.description: Erase all 16 slots
output: C clear; C set on no RTC

slots.name: VdpInfo
slots.summary: Card found at boot → A=VDP_FW, X=VDP_CAPS, Y=$AC; carry set if none
slots.description: What the probe found
output: A = VDP_FW (STAT5), X = VDP_CAPS (STAT6), Y = VDP_ID ($AC); with no card A = X = Y = 0 and carry set

slots.name: VdpWriteReg
slots.summary: Write register (A=value, X=0-127), keeping VID_MODE and the LxCTRL shadows
slots.description: Write a VDP register, keeping the Kernal's records of it
input: A = value, X = register (0-127)
output: carry set, and nothing written, if no card or X > 127
notes: A VMODE write sets VID_MODE: the mode, with b7 (disturbed) set when it takes
the card to Text or the legacy submode from anything else, so that only
InitVideo can say the Text console is intact.  L0CTRL and L1CTRL, which read
back as nothing, are kept in VDP_L0CTRL_SHADOW and VDP_L1CTRL_SHADOW.
Preserves: X, Y

slots.name: VdpSetMode
slots.summary: Write VMODE (A=1-4); carry set if out of range
slots.description: Set VMODE: 1 Text, 2 Compact, 3 Graphics, 4 Full
input: A = mode (1-4)
output: carry set, and nothing written, if no card or A is out of range
notes: Only the register (and VID_MODE, as VdpWriteReg keeps it): the tables, layers
and sprites are the caller's to lay out.  The Text console proper is
InitVideo.

slots.name: VdpPoke
slots.summary: Write VRAM byte A at X/Y = address lo/hi (all 64 KB)
slots.description: Write one byte anywhere in VRAM
input: A = value, X = address low, Y = address high ($0000-$FFFF)
output: carry set, and nothing written, if no card

slots.name: VdpPeek
slots.summary: Read VRAM byte at X/Y = address lo/hi → A
slots.description: Read one byte anywhere in VRAM
input: X = address low, Y = address high ($0000-$FFFF)
output: A = the byte; carry set, and nothing read, if no card

slots.name: VdpSetPalette
slots.description: Set one palette entry in VRAM, at $FC00 + 2 * entry
input: X = entry (0-255), A = $0R, Y = $GB
output: carry set, and nothing written, if no card
notes: The card takes the write into its palette at once (SPEC §11).  $FC00 is where
InitVideo puts PALBASE; a program that moves PALBASE writes its own.

slots.name: WaitVBlank
slots.summary: Return at the start of the next vertical blank (STAT0 untouched)
slots.description: Return at the start of the next vertical blank
notes: Polls STAT3 b0 on port A: waits while the display is in blanking, then until
it is, and puts STATSEL_A back to 0.  Not STAT0's F: reading STAT0 clears
F, OVF and COL and the STAT1 latches a program or its interrupt handler may
be relying on, and this leaves them all as they were.
No card: waits 2 cs through SysDelay instead, so a loop paced by it still
runs at about the speed it would, and returns carry set.

slots.name: VdpLoadFile
slots.summary: Load named file (STR_PTR) into VRAM at FS_IO_ADDR, exactly FS_FILE_SIZE bytes
slots.description: Load a named file from the current disk into VRAM
input: STR_PTR = filename, FS_IO_ADDR = VRAM address
output: Carry clear = loaded, FS_FILE_SIZE = bytes written
Carry set = no video card (nothing read), or not found or read error
modifies: Flags, A, X, Y, CF_LBA, CF_BUF_PTR, XFER_REMAIN, FS_SECTOR_BUF
notes: Streams the file through port A to FS_IO_ADDR, anywhere in the 64 KB, and
writes exactly its FS_FILE_SIZE bytes: the rest of the last sector is read
and dropped, so a table loaded here cannot spill into the one after it.

slots.name: VdpLoadFont
slots.summary: Copy built-in font A into L0PAT and wait for it
slots.description: Load one of the card's built-in fonts into layer 0's pattern table
input: A = font ID
output: carry set, and nothing written, if no card or A is not $00
notes: Writes the font ID to FONT (SPEC §7), which copies it to L0PAT x $800 as that
register stands at the write, and waits for the copy: a pending load lands at
the line start where vertical blank begins, before STAT3 b0 sets, so
WaitVBlank returning is the completion.  STAT0 is not read.  The only font
STAT6 b7 promises is $00 (VDP_FONT_CP437), so any other ID is refused rather
than written as a command that would do nothing.

slots.name: VdpSprite
slots.summary: Sprite X = 0-63 ← VDP_P0-P3 = Y, X lo, pattern, attributes (table at $2000)
slots.description: Write one sprite's four attribute bytes
input: X = sprite (0-63), VDP_P0 = Y, VDP_P1 = X bits 7:0, VDP_P2 = pattern,
VDP_P3 = attributes (b7 = X bit 8, b6 priority, b5:4 flips, b3:0 sub-palette; SPEC §10)
output: carry set, and nothing written, if no card or X > 63
notes: The attribute table is taken to be at VRAM $2000 (SPRATTR = $40), where
BASIC's SCREEN 1-3 puts it; a program that moves SPRATTR writes its sprites
with VdpPoke.  Sets VID_MODE b7 (disturbed).
Preserves: X

slots.name: VdpSetScroll
slots.summary: Layer X = 0-1 scroll: A = x lo, Y = y, VDP_P0 = x bit 8
slots.description: Scroll a layer
input: X = layer (0-1), A = x bits 7:0, Y = y, VDP_P0 = x bit 8 (0 or not)
output: carry set, and nothing written, if no card or X > 1
notes: Writes LxSCRX, LxSCRY, and LxCTRL with b6 = X bit 8 and its other bits from
the shadow.  Sets VID_MODE b7 (disturbed).

slots.name: VdpLayer
slots.description: Show or hide a layer
input: X = layer (0-1), A = 0 to hide, anything else to show
output: carry set, and nothing written, if no card or X > 1
notes: Sets or clears LxCTRL b4, keeping its other bits from the shadow.  Sets
VID_MODE b7 (disturbed).

slots.name: VdpStatus
slots.summary: Read status register X = 0-15 on port A → A
slots.description: Read a status register through port A
input: X = status register (0-15)
output: A = its value; carry set, and nothing read, if no card or X > 15
notes: Selects STATn with STATSEL_A, reads it, and puts STATSEL_A back to 0 without
reading STAT0.  Reading STAT0 itself clears its flags, and STAT1 its
latches, as SPEC §6 says.
Preserves: X, Y
